proposals.evidence: Turner sajya/sajja explicitly gives Gujarati sājũ sound/healthy and regional good/in-good-order meanings. These neighbouring Bhili/Bareli/Noiri/Vasavi hāj-/hādz- good responses are qualified comparisons with that health/goodness family, retaining local s-to-h realization and adjectival extensions. The identification does not treat the similar right-hand meaning as the elicited sense.
